fix: Do not clone the Vec per frame. Snapshot only the count and clone each Rc inside the loop, so no Vec is allocated: `let count = SCHEDULER.with(|s| s.borrow().persistent_callbacks.len()); for index in 0..count { let callback = SCHEDULER.with(|s| s.borrow().persistent_callbacks.get(index).cloned()); if let Some(callback) = callback { callback(now); } }`. The count snapshot keeps the current semantics (callbacks added during this loop run next frame). Remove the `(persistent, post)` tuple accordingly and keep the `post_frame_callbacks` take as is.

Collect into a scratch Vec kept in `Scheduler` (new field `ticking: Vec<Rc<TickerState>>`, initialised empty) instead of a fresh Vec each frame. `let mut tickers = SCHEDULER.with(|s| std::mem::take(&mut s.borrow_mut().ticking)); SCHEDULER.with(|s| { let mut s = s.borrow_mut(); s.tickers.retain(|t| t.strong_count() > 0); tickers.extend(s.tickers.iter().filter_map(Weak::upgrade).filter(|t| t.active.get())); }); for ticker in tickers.drain(..) { ticker.tick(now); } SCHEDULER.with(|s| s.borrow_mut().ticking = tickers);`. The take/restore keeps re-entrant ticks safe (they touch `tickers`, not the scratch), and the buffer keeps its capacity across frames.

Add a fallible form and keep the panic only as its documented wrapper: `pub fn try_set_time_dilation(dilation: f64) -> Result<(), InvalidTimeDilation>` returning `Err(InvalidTimeDilation(dilation))` when `!(dilation.is_finite() && dilation > 0.0)`, with a `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct InvalidTimeDilation(pub f64);` plus Display/Error impls. Then `pub fn set_time_dilation(dilation: f64) { try_set_time_dilation(dilation).expect("time dilation was validated by the documented contract") }` with the existing `# Panics` doc kept. Re-export the new error from the crate root and mention the pair in the CHANGELOG.

fn interpolate(from: Self, to: Self, t: f32) -> Self {
        (from as f32 + (to - from) as f32 * t).round() as i32
fix: Compute the difference in a wide type so it cannot overflow: `(f64::from(from) + (f64::from(to) - f64::from(from)) * f64::from(t)).round() as i32`. Rust float-to-int `as` saturates, so the result stays in range. The i32 subtraction `to - from` panics in debug and wraps in release when the endpoints span more than i32::MAX (e.g. i32::MIN to i32::MAX).
